title: 2022 AMC 12B Problem 16
statement:
Suppose \(x\) and \(y\) are positive real numbers such that

\[x^y = 2^{64}\] and \[(\log_2 x)^{\log_2 y} = 2^7.\]

What is the greatest possible value of \(\log_2 y?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(a = \log_2 x\) and \(b = \log_2 y.\) Taking \(\log_2\) of \(x^y = 2^{64}\) gives \(y \log_2 x = 64,\) i.e. \(a \cdot 2^b = 2^6.\)

Taking \(\log_2\) of the second equation gives \(b \log_2 a = 7,\) so \(a = 2^{\frac{7}{b}}.\) Substituting, \(2^{\frac{7}{b}} \cdot 2^b = 2^6,\) so \(b + \dfrac7b = 6,\) i.e. \(b^2 - 6b + 7 = 0.\)

Thus \(b = 3 \pm \sqrt2,\) and the greatest value of \(\log_2 y\) is \(3 + \sqrt2.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Let \(a = \log_2 x\) and \(b = \log_2 y;\) take \(\log_2\) of both equations
You get \(a \cdot 2^b = 2^6\) and \(a = 2^{\frac{7}{b}};\) combine to form a quadratic in \(b\)
